w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Arctic District (D17) LNM17-248B89
w.t:
SECTOR ANCHORAGE, TERRITORIAL SEA - SECTOR ANCHORAGE, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA)
General / Hazards To Navigation / Obstructions
ConocoPhillips Alaska, Inc. (CPAI) plans to conduct marine ocean and seabed characterization studies near Oliktok Point. Studies will include buoy installation, tide gauge installation, bathymetric surveys, and navigational hazard surveys during the open water seasons of 2024, 2025, 2026, and 2027. Temporary monitoring equipment will be placed in the area to support the studies. This request is specific to activities planned for the 2026 season; an LMN will be submitted in subsequent years as needed. Buoy installation includes the deployment and recovery of three wave buoys offshore of Oliktok Point during the 2026 open water season. Preliminary buoy locations are included in Table 1 and shown on the attached map; final buoy locations may vary by about 1 nautical mile from the preliminary locations based on planning with local vessel operators and conditions encountered in the field. Buoy 1 will be installed in shallow water, approximately 5 to 10 feet deep. Buoys 2 and 3 will be installed in deeper water, approximately 25 to 30 feet deep. All buoys will float on the surface. Final buoy locations, depths, and water depth will be recorded and submitted within two days of deployment. Each Spotter buoy will be moored to the seafloor and will have a spar buoy equipped with an LED strobe light to alert mariners. Buoys will be deployed in late-July or early- August and recovered in late-September to mid-October. One tide gauge will be installed at or near the Oliktok Point during the 2026 open water season. The tide gauge will consist of a pressure transducer located in a water depth of three to five feet, a cable to shore, and a data recorder onshore. The pressure transducer will be located about 20 feet from shore and will be mounted on a ¾ inch pipe that sticks up above the water approximately 3 feet. The pipe will be driven 2 to 3 feet into the seabed using a post drive and will be clearly marked for safety. The onshore data recorder will be kept in a weather resistant container (e.g. cooler or bucket) and secured to the gravel bag jetty on the west side of Oliktok Point. A survey staff will be installed next to the pressure transducer to provide manual readout. The staff will also be attached to a ¾ inch pipe driven into the seabed in the same manner as the pressure transducer. The tide gauge will be installed at the beginning of the open-water season. The tide gauge and associated materials will be removed prior to freeze up. The stake on which the tide gauge is mounted could present a hazard for small boats transiting near the beach. Mariners should reduce wake when transiting the area and maintain a distance of at least 100 feet from the stake in the water and the data recorder on shore. Work is planned to begin as early as July 10, 2026. Please contact Miranda Buckmaster at (907) 263-4868 or miranda.buckmaster@conocophillips.com should you have any questions or require additional information.
USCG Arctic District Local Notice to Mariners 47/2026

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Arctic District (D17) LNM17-1B611E
w.t:
SECTOR ANCHORAGE, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA) - PRINCE WILLIAM SOUND
General / Hazards To Navigation / Hazards
Location: 61-10.32N 148-28.50W 61-10.24N 148-03.45W 61-02.28N 148-03.45W 60-55.81N 148-28.99W 61-10.32N 148-28.50W The State of Alaka is issuing routine updates on the Barry Arm Landslide Tsunami risk. This threat is located in Barry Arm and has the potential to create a tsunami if/when a landslide is generated that impacts the water in Barry Arm. If/when this occurs localized wave heights will be very hazardous in Barry Arm and Harriman Fjord. Port Wells and Passage Canal will also see inundation and strong, unusual currents for hours following an event. The geologic makeup of the area is similar to Alaskan locations where two previous landslide caused tsunamis occurred, in Lituya Bay (1958) and Icy Bay (2015), both causing extremely large but localized tsunamis. Mariners should maintain vigilance when in the vicinity of Barry Arm or nearby waters and be prepared to depart the area if any unusual geologic activity is observed. Studies are being conducted and the situation is being monitored to allow for a better understanding of the potential results of a slide. Additional information is available at https://dggs.alaska.gov/hazards/barry-arm-landslide.html.
Valid 2024-10-28 to 2029-10-27.
USCG Arctic District Local Notice to Mariners 47/2026

Location: 38-59.52N 076-22.63W Bridge Name: William Preston Lane Junior Memorial Eastbound Bridge Mariners are advised that an engineering firm, on behalf of Maryland Transportation Authority, will be performing inspections on the main navigation spans of the William Preston Lane Junior Memorial Eastbound Bridge, across the Chesapeake Bay, mile 138.0, near Annapolis, MD, and the William Preston Lane Junior Memorial Westbound Bridge, across the Chesapeake Bay, mile 138.1, near Annapolis, MD. The inspections which began November 2026, will continue to be conducted from 9 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.; Monday-Friday; through January 15, 2027. An under-bridge inspection vehicle and work platform will continue to be located in and around the bridges. During the work hours from December 7, 2026, through December 18, 2026, and from January 4, 2027, through January 15, 2027, the under-bridge inspection vehicle and work platform will be within the navigational channels of the William Preston Lane Junior Memorial Eastbound Bridge and William Preston Lane Junior Memorial Westbound Bridge which will reduce the vertical clearance of the bridges by approximately 5 feet. Vessels that can safely transit through the bridges during periods with a reduced vertical clearance may continue to do so at any time. Vessels with air drafts exceeding 174 feet may not transit through the bridges during the above periods of reduced vertical clearance. Work vessels may continue to be reached on VHF-FM channels 13 and 16. The project foreman can continue to be reached at (443) 310-4743 or (410) 924-7587. w.t:
SECTOR VIRGINIA, EXCLUSIVE ECONOMIC ZONE (EEZ) - SECTOR VIRGINIA, TERRITORIAL SEA
General / LAA / RNA / Safety Zone
MSIB 103-26 November 24, 2026 SUMMARY: The COTP Sector Virginia will elevate Port Conditions to a MODIFIED ZULU at 2:00 p.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in response to forecasted severe weather affecting Norfolk Harbor Entrance, Virginia portions of the Chesapeake Bay, and Virginia ocean inlets, in accordance with 33 CFR. § 165.520. During severe weather, vessel movement, port operations, and emergency-response capabilities, including Search and Rescue, may be impacted. AREAS OF CONCERN: Chesapeake Bay from the MD/VA state line through the Virginia Capes and including Thimble Shoal Channel, and all ocean inlets. ACTIONS: Port Condition X-RAY is currently in effect for Sector Virginia. Per regulation, all vessels and facilities must prepare for potential storm impacts. Port condition YANKEE will not be established for this weather event. Sector Virginia COTP will establish a MODIFIED ZULU port condition. MODIFIED ACTIONS: Beginning at 2:00 p.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, Inbound vessels requiring state pilotage must have the state pilot aboard by 2:00 p.m. Outbound vessels requiring state pilotage must disembark the state pilot before 2:00 p.m. During modified Port Condition ZULU, vessels that do not require a state pilot may not transit through the Virginia Capes. Vessel movements west of the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel will be limited to vessels of 500 gross tons or less to support tug movements and assistance. Cargo operations west of the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel may continue as normal. All vessels should follow the recommended precautionary measures for storm preparation. Moored Vessels Moored vessels should have additional mooring lines available to reinforce existing lines as needed. Vessels should also have an outboard anchor ready for use and spare mooring lines or wires readily available. Anchored Vessels Anchored vessels should have a second anchor ready for deployment, remain prepared to get underway within 15 minutes, and use available drag-circle alarm features on installed navigation equipment. Any deviation from the requirements of modified Port Condition ZULU must be approved by the COTP. Marine Broadcasts will announce subsequent Port Condition updates. Resumption of normal Marine Transportation System operations is predicated on actual storm conditions, and any post-storm assessments, during Port Condition RECOVERY. Anticipate channel assessments to be conducted at 3:00p.m. on Thursday November 26, 2026 to determine port reconstitution. COMMUNICATIONS: Direct all inquiries and any emergencies to the 24 / 7 Sector Virginia Command Center via VHF CH 16 or (877) 722-5727.

General / Bridges / Maintenance
Location: 38-59.46N 074-50.00W Bridge Name: 47 State Route Bridge Mariners are advised that an engineering firm, on behalf of New Jersey Department of Transportation, will continue to be performing maintenance on the highway drawbridge 47 State Route (George Redding) Bridge, across the New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway (NJICW), Grassy Sound Channel, mile 108.9, at Wildwood, NJ. The maintenance which began in September 2026, will continue to be conducted from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Monday-Friday; through March 31, 2027. A 40-foot work barge and a tugboat will continue to be located in and around the vicinity of the bridge. During the work hours, the work barge will continue to be located within the entirety of the navigation channel of the bridge to provide access for structural steel repairs to the bascule span. Vessels may continue to safely transit through the bridge, if at least a one-hour prior notice is given to the project foreman. Maintenance personnel, equipment and vessels will continue to relocate from the moveable span and navigable channel, upon request. Work vessels may continue to be reached on VHF-FM channel 13 and 16. The project foreman can continue to be reached at (609) 579-8147. Mariners should use extreme caution navigating through the area. During the maintenance period, the bridge will be maintained in the closed-to-navigation position to perform structural steel repairs to the bridge bascule span. The bridge will remain in the closed-to-navigation position Monday through Friday, from 7 a.m. on Monday through 4 p.m. on Friday, from January 4, 2027, through February 26, 2027. The bridge will not be able to open for emergencies. There is no immediate alternative route for vessels unable to pass through the bridge in the closed position. Vessels able to pass through the bridge in the closed position may do so at any time. At all other times, the drawbridge will operate in accordance with the operating regulations set out in Title 33 Code of Federal Regulations Part 117.5. Mariners should adjust their transits accordingly and should use caution when transiting the area. MSI #52664
Valid 2026-11-23 to 2027-04-09.

SECTOR DELAWARE BAY, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA) - CAPE MAY INLET
General / Bridges / Proposal
Location: 38-57.35N 074-52.45W Bridge Name: 621 County Route Bridge All interested parties are notified that the Commander, Coast Guard East District has received a proposal from the Cape May County Bridge Commission with plans for replacement of an existing highway drawbridge across a navigable waterway of the United States. WATERWAY AND LOCATION: Middle Thorofare, New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway (NJICW), at mile 112.2, at approximate location [38-57.35N 074-52.45W], and the Upper Thorofare, at mile 0.0, at approximate location [38-57.32N 074-52.62W] near Lower Township, Cape May County, NJ. CHARACTER OF WORK: The proposed project is to replace the Two-Mile drawbridge, located on County Route 621 (Ocean Drive), across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, with a fixed bridge that will carry County Route 621 (Ocean Drive), across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, and Upper Thorofare, near Lower Township, Cape May County, NJ. The purpose of the project is to address structural, geometric, carrying capacity, and operational deficiencies of the Cape May County Bridge Commission-owned bridge located across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, on the Ocean Drive Causeway, and to provide safe, efficient, and reliable passage for all modes of transportation. The existing drawbridge across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, has a horizontal clearance of 50.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 23.00 feet above mean high water in the closed position and unlimited vertical clearance in the open position. The replacement bridge will be a fixed bridge across Middle Thorofare, NJICW, and Upper Thorofare. The portion of the replacement bridge across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, will provide a horizontal clearance of 80.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 80.00 feet above mean high water. The portion of the replacement bridge across Upper Thorofare, will provide a horizontal clearance of 50.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 49.73 feet above mean high water. A copy of Preliminary Public Notice D05PPN-06-2026, which describes the proposal in detail, can be obtained by calling (571) 607-6762 or by viewing at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/public-notice-for-bridges-active (select East District). Comments will be received for the record at the address in the header or via email at (D5Portsmouth-BridgesPublicNotice@uscg.mil) no later than December 4, 2026.
Valid 2026-11-04 to 2026-12-05.
USCG East District Local Notice to Mariners 47/2026

--- MSIB 32-26 - Potential Unexploded Ordnance (UXO) Hazard Gulf of America - Fort Pickens, FL --- The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is conducting feasibility studies under the CERCLA process to assess hazards associated with historical munitions to include potential unexploded ordnance (UXO) in the vicinity of Fort Pickens, Pensacola, FL. Due to historical usage of this area, the U.S. Coast Guard advises mariners of potential UXOs located within the Gulf of America and Pensacola Bay, near Santa Rosa Island, Fort Pickens, FL. UXOs should be considered extremely dangerous. If touched, moved, or disturbed, these items may detonate, causing severe injury, death, or property damage. Mariners are strongly urged not to anchor or conduct any bottom-disturbing activities within High Use Areas (HUA) and should exercise caution when conducting activities in the Low Use Areas (LUA). Reference diagrams, provided in the hard copy version of MSIB 32-26, identify Low Use Areas (LUA) in green and High Use Areas (HUA) in orange. If a mariner encounters a UXO, please contact 911 to report the location that it was found. Concerned parties may report any hazardous conditions to the U.S. Coast Guard Sector Mobile Command Center at (251) 266-5888. Additional information is available at: https://www.saj.usace.army.mil/FortPickens/

General / MSIB
--- Marine Safety Alert 02-24 - Inspections and Compliance Directorate --- DANGEROUS BYCATCH FROM DISCARDED MUNITIONS REMAINS A PRESENT DAY HAZARD --- This Safety Alert is being issued to raise awareness of lurking hazards caused by discarded munitions, which often contain active explosives or chemical agents. Although the practice of dumping munitions into the sea ceased in 1970, a significant amount remains hidden in coastal waters, posing a safety hazard to commercial fisherman, dredge operators, and others who trawl and work the ocean floor. Recently, a deckhand on a clamming vessel was severely burned when a canister was dredged up and brought onboard with clams and other debris. The canister likely contained mustard gas or another blistering agent, but did not display any obvious visual, audible, or odor indicators of discharging content. A member of the crew discovered the canister and threw it back overboard. Several hours later he developed a severe rash that required professional medical treatment. Mustard gas is a chemical weapon developed during World War I. Millions of pounds of this product, other chemical weapons, bombs, torpedoes, artillery shells, and munitions were routinely disposed of and remain in U.S. coastal waters. Although many munition dump areas are well marked on navigation charts, numerous areas where munitions were discarded remain unmarked. There is also evidence suggesting that munitions were frequently “short dumped,” meaning dumped outside of the designated areas by contractors hired to take them to the intended locations. The Coast Guard previously issued Safety Alert 11-16 and Safety Alert 6-10 on this same topic and continues to strongly recommend that persons involved in the fishing and dredging industries: Review their navigational charts to ensure the areas in which they are trawling or dredging are not near labeled “Explosives Dumping Areas.” Such areas must be given wide berth and seafarers should recognize that surface bottoms change and that objects can move significant distances from their original disposal areas. Review and follow recommendations from the Maritime Industry 3Rs Explosive Safety Guide. Carefully record the position of any munitions encountered and returned to the sea. Immediately report discovery to the National Response Center, at (800) 424-8802 to ensure a proper response and potential recovery. Alternatively, the local U.S. Coast Guard unit may be notified via VHF-FM Channel 16. This Safety Alert is provided for informational purposes only and does not relieve any domestic or international safety, operational, or material requirement. Developed by the Office of Commercial Vessel Compliance (CG-CVC) and distributed by the Office of Investigations and Casualty Analysis (CG-INV). Questions may be submitted to HQS-SMB-CGINV@uscg.mil.

Mobile River Channel - Safety Zone ---  To: May 2030 --- The Captain of the Port (COTP) Mobile is enforcing a fixed Safety Zone in accordance with 33 CFR 165.T08-1214 surrounding the M/V EX ENTERPRISE as the vessel is moored at a receiving facility located on the Mobile River at 701 South Royal Street, Mobile, AL. This Safety Zone is necessary to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from hazards associated with a dismantling operation, including removal of hazardous and regulated materials, and continuous work activity on and around the hull. All navigable waters of the Mobile River along the RDB will be designated as a fixed moored Safety Zone and will be bound by the following coordinates: 30-40.57N 088-02.27W, 30-40.57N 088-02.22W, 30-40.30N 088-02.08W, 30-40.32N 088-02.27W and north along the shoreline to the point of origin. The Safety Zone does not include waters within the Mobile River Federal Channel; therefore, no impact to commercial vessel traffic is anticipated. This zone will be enforced for the duration of dismantling operations, and remain in effect until the COTP determines the area no longer presents safety concerns. The dismantlement project is expected to progress to a safe stage approximately May 2030. In the event this fixed moored Safety Zone is no longer needed before May 2030, mariners will be notified through a Marine Safety Information Bulletin (MSIB) or other appropriate means. No person may enter or remain in the zone unless authorized by the COTP or a designated representative. Those in the Safety Zone must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative. To seek permission to enter, mariners can contact the COTP or the COTP’s representative on VHF-FM Channel 16.

Alabama River - In accordance with Section 7-11 of the ACT Master Water Control Manual dated April 2022, full navigation channel availability on the Alabama River is dependent upon channel maintenance, seasonal flow conditions, and basin status. Flows for navigation are most needed in the unregulated portion of the lower Alabama River below Claiborne Lock and Dam. Alabama Power Company (APC) operates its reservoirs on the Coosa and Tallapoosa Rivers to provide a minimum navigation flow target in the Alabama River at Montgomery, Alabama. Basin status criteria are correlated to APC Drought Operations (ADROP) updates which monitors drought triggers related to basin inflow, state line flow on the Coosa River between Georgia and Alabama, as well as composite storage availability within the APC projects. These updates are provided monthly on the first and third Tuesday. Below is the most recent ADROP update provided by Alabama Power Company on October 20, 2026: *ADROP UPDATE* - Low Basin Inflow: FALSE - - Low State Line Flow: FALSE - - Low Composite Storage: FALSE - - Montgomery Flow Target: 4,200 cfs daily average (NOTE: ADROP requires one drought intensity level change per cycle regardless of the number of triggers enacted when exiting drought operations.) - - Current Operations: Drought Intensity Level 1 - Currently, based on profile survey conducted on 04JUN2024, a 10 ft tailwater elevation near Claiborne Lock is required to provide a 9 ft navigation channel on the lower Alabama River. A modified depth of 7.5 ft navigable draft can be provided with a tailwater elevation of 8.5 ft at the Claiborne Lock and Dam. Commercial mariners should check water levels daily and schedule lockage appointments by calling the Claiborne Lock Supervisor at (251) 282-4575. Tailwater elevations below Claiborne Lock and Dam can be viewed at: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-02428401

w.t:
NEW ORLEANS TO BATON ROUGE - LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER
General / MSIB
The U.S. Coast Guard COTP Lower Mississippi River has issued a low water Safety Advisory between approximate Miles 869.0 and 303.0. The USACE maintained depths and widths, may not be attainable on all buoy lines. It is recommended that mariners monitor all gauge readings for safe navigation. The U.S. Coast Guard COTP Lower Mississippi River, with the concurrence of the Lower Mississippi River Committee, recommends the following limits for tows: Southbound tows between Miles 869.0 and 585.0 Drafts no greater than 11.0 feet. Barges to be configured no more than 6 wide. Southbound tows between Miles 585.0 and 303.0 Drafts no greater than 11.6 feet. Barges to be configured no more than 7 wide. w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Northeast District (D1) LNM01-7551B6
w.t:
LONG ISLAND SOUND EASTERN PART - MATTITUCK INLET
General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Dredging
Mariners are advised that the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is conducting maintenance dredging operations within the Federal Navigation Channel at Mattituck Inlet, New York. The project is necessary to restore the authorized dimensions of the federal channel and is being completed within an environmentally restricted dredging window. The dredging operation utilizes floating pipeline and associated equipment extending across portions of the channel. Vessel transits through the work area require suspension of dredging operations and the disassembly and relocation of equipment to allow safe passage. Frequent interruptions have significantly delayed project progress and may prevent completion of the federally authorized maintenance project within the available work window. To facilitate the safe and efficient completion of dredging operations while preserving access for commercial and recreational waterway users, a voluntary vessel traffic management scheme will be implemented during active dredging operations. Designated Transit Windows Vessels are strongly encouraged to plan departures and arrivals during the following daily transit periods: 0530 - 0730 (Morning departures) 1200 - 1300 (Midday transit window) 1430 - 1530 (Afternoon arrivals and departures) Dredging operations will occur during the day between 6 A.M. and 6 P.M. Outside of these designated transit periods, dredging operations will continue and vessel traffic may experience delays while safe passage arrangements are coordinated. Mariners requiring passage outside of the designated transit windows should contact the dredge on VHF-FM Channel 13/16 in advance of arrival to coordinate safe transit through the work area. Every effort will be made to accommodate vessel traffic while minimizing disruptions to dredging operations. All vessels transiting the area are requested to proceed at a safe speed, minimize wake, maintain a vigilant lookout, follow instructions provided by on-scene personnel, and monitor VHF-FM Channel 13/16 while transiting the work area. This traffic management scheme will remain in effect during active dredging operations from 19 November 2026 through approximately 21 December 2026, subject to weather conditions, operational requirements, and project progress. These measures are expected to remain in effect through completion of dredging operations, currently anticipated on or about 21 December 2026, subject to weather and operational conditions. Nothing in this voluntary traffic management scheme is intended to delay or impede vessels responding to emergencies involving the safety of life or property. Mariners requiring immediate transit due to a medical emergency, vessel casualty, loss of propulsion, or other emergent circumstance should contact the dredge and/or U.S. Coast Guard Sector Long Island Sound as soon as practicable to coordinate safe passage through the work area. For additional information, contact U.S. Coast Guard Sector Long Island Sound waterway management at 475-355-5336 or email SECLISSPWMarineEvent@uscg.mil.
Valid 2026-11-19 to 2026-12-22.

w.t:
LONG ISLAND SOUND EASTERN PART - NEW HAVEN HARBOR
General / MSIB
Location: 41-16.93N 072-54.93W SUMMARY: The U.S. Anny Corps of Engineers (USACE). New England District, will be conducting dredging operations in support of the New Haven Harbor Improvement Project in New Haven, Connecticut. Mariners are advised to use caution, maintain a proper lookout. and communicate early with the dredging vessel when operating in or near the project area. SITUATION: The New Haven Harbor Improvement Project will modernize approximately 5.5 miles of the federal navigation channel serving the deep-water terminals of New Haven. Great Lakes Dock and Dredge Company, under contract with USACE, is expected to conduct work over two dredging cycles. The first one beginning in October 2026 and continuing through March 2027, and the second cycle beginning in October 2027 and continuing through March 2028. Operations are planned to take place 24 hours a clay, 7 days a week. Planned improvements include deepening the entrance channel, main channel, maneuvering area, and turning basin from 35 feet to 40 feet; widening the entrance channel from 500 feet to 600 feet outside the breakwaters; widening the channel bend between the breakwaters from 560 feet to 800 feet; widening the main channel inside the harbor from 400 feet to 500 feet; and optimizing the turning basin for larger vessels. Dredging operations may affect normal vessel movement, maneuvering, and transit within New Haven Harbor. Mariners should anticipate the presence of dredging equipment and associated support vessels within the federal navigation channel and surrounding work areas. Vessels looking to transit the area are urged to contact the dredge early to arrange safe passage and to maintain a proper lookout when navigating near operations. COMMUNICATIONS: For urgent safety-of-life matters, please contact the Sector Long Island Sound Command Center on VHF-FM Channel 16 or call (866) 299-8031. Working Vessels will monitor channels 13, 16, and 79. Additionally, please check USCG Navigation Center oflen for updates to the public from the US Coast Guard. Questions regarding this bulletin may be directed to Lieutenant Joel Chapman. ChiefofWaterways Management Division at (475) 355-5336 or email SECLlSSPWMarineEvent@uscg.mil.
Valid 2026-10-26 to 2027-04-01.

General / Naval Activity / Military Operations
The Navy will conduct tactical boat operations on the 20th of November 2026 on the water along the western side of US Naval Magazine Indian Island, during the hours of 0900-1500. The exercise area is located from the southern portion of Crane Point at 48-02.92N 122-44.52W extending westward to 48-02.92N 122-44.88W, extending NNW to 48-04.32N 122-45.61W, and extending to the N and NE encompassing 500 meters standoff from the Portable Security Barrier (PSB) system to Walan Point. It is required that all vessels maintain a safe distance in all directions from the northern edge of the Ammunition Pier extending from Walan Point extending westward to the identified coordinates and south of Crane Point area as well as 500 yards from the vessels engaged in exercises. w.t:
WILLIAMETTE
General / Bridges
Bridge Notice The Coast Guard has issued a public notice announcing a permit application from the Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT) for the approval of location and plans for the construction of a temporary bridge at waterway mile 84.5, across the Willamette River, near Salem, OR, at 44°56'41.6"N, 123°02'36.6"W. ODOT is proposing seismic retrofit of the Center Street Bridge which is one of two Willamette River crossings in the Salem area. The project is downtown Salem adjacent to and above Wallace Marine Park and Riverfront Park, above the Willamette River, and over local streets and an active railroad track. Following a major seismic event, this seismically vulnerable bridge would take years to repair or replace due to the size of the crossing, leading to substantial delay in recovery of the area and resulting in additional challenges to the statewide post-earthquake recovery effort. Completing a seismic retrofit will improve the safety of the bridge and speed of recovery of the area after a major seismic event. This bridge permit application is for a temporary work bridge to support seismic retrofit work on the existing Center Street Bridge structure. The Coast Guard has confirmed that no new bridge permit will be required for the Center Street Bridge itself. The complete public notice (numbered 05-26) including: a summary of project impacts, a map of the location, and plans for the proposed bridge can be viewed and printed from website https://navcen.uscg.gov/public-notices-for-bridges-active-by-district? district=13&subdistrict=n. Comments should be submitted on or before December 2, 2026. Comments received will be made part of the case record.
USCG Northwest District Local Notice to Mariners 47/2026

w.t:

General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Boring and Core Samples
The Interstate Bridge Replacement Program will be conducting geotechnical investigations west of the existing Interstate 5 Bridge across the Columbia River between Vancouver, WA and Portland, OR at Columbia (RM 106.5) from 02 Nov 2026 – 31 Jan 2027. The work will infringe on the Alternate Barge Channel South, Alternative Barge Channel North, and the Vancouver to The Dalles Channel (lift span). The Tug South Creek and Barge Mark 12 will be on station and will reduce available horizontal clearances. The normal amount of horizontal clearance available at these channels will be reduced, and vessels are advised to use alternate channels if horizontal clearance is not sufficient in the channels. Only one channel will be reduced at any one time. Mariners are requested to maintain an appropriate distance and create no wake within 200 feet. Tug operator will be monitoring VHF Channels 13 and 16. During non-working hours the barge will remain on station with al-round white lights on all 4 corners, pursuant to CFR 83.30. w.t:
SALMONBAY
General / Bridges
WASHINGTON – LAKE WASHINGTON SHIP CANAL – SHILSHOLE BAY – Bridge notice (Revised) Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway Company (BNSF) will be performing heavy rail maintenance/construction on the Salmon Bay Railroad Bridge (BRDG UID 31177) (AKA BNSF Bridge 6.3), mile 0.1, across the Lake Washington Ship Canal in Seattle, Washington. The construction work requires the draw of the subject bridge to be closed from 02 November 2026 to 25 November 2026. This draw closure corresponds with the USACE’s large Hiram M. Chittenden Lock closure. The Coast Guard has approved a temporary deviation to the operating schedule that governs the Salmon Bay Railroad Bridge from 0600 on 02 November 2026 to 1600 on 25 November 2026. The draw will be able to open from 8 A.M. to 8 P.M on 14 - 18 November 2026, if a 24-hour notice is given to the bridge operator. The subject bridge provides 43 feet of vertical clearance in the closed-to-navigation position at mean higher high water. Vessels which do not require a bridge opening may continue to transit beneath the bridge during this closure period. This construction requires barges in the navigation channel during the same time as USACE’s annual lock closure and maintenance to minimize impacts. A crane and material barge will be positioned in the water to service the work of erecting temporary trusses that are required to execute the counterweight change out. During this timeframe, access on the southern channel to the small locks will be in operation during the large lock closure. A construction zone will be established for mariners to navigate around at minimum safe speed. The subject bridge will not be able to open for emergencies, and there is no immediate alternate route for vessels to pass. For more information on this draw bridge closure contact Travis Woodley at travis.woodley@bnsf.com or (682) 978-3311.

MSIB 004-26 Quiet Sound Voluntary Slowdown https://www.pacificarea.uscg.mil/Our-Organization/Northwest-District/District-Staff/dp/dpw/notices/ The Quiet Sound voluntary commercial vessel slowdown in Admiralty Inlet aims to reduce underwater noise in Southern Resident killer whale critical habitat. The 2025-26 slowdown will be in effect starting at 0001 PST on 3 September 2026 and will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PST on 31 January 2027, at the latest, depending on orca presence. More information can be found at: https://quietsound.org/admiralty-inlet-slowdown. When in effect, the slowdown requests all inbound and outbound commercial vessels transiting through the slowdown zone not exceed the following speeds through water when safe and operationally feasible: 11 knots – General cargo, bulkers and tankers 14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels The voluntary vessel slowdown takes place in the inbound and outbound lanes of the shipping lanes within these boundaries: Northwest: a line drawn from Pt Hudson (48-07.04N 122-44.93W) to Admiralty Head (48-09.25N 122-40.77W) Northeast: a line drawn from Randall Pt (47-58.99N 122-21.17W) to Mukilteo Light (47-56.89N 122-18.48W) South: a line drawn from Apple Cove Pt (47-48-55.926N, 122-28.51.186W) to Edwards Pt (47-48.20N 122-23.70W) Speed transition zones are in place about 5 nautical miles prior to entering the slowdown area. Any directions from Puget Sound Vessel Traffic Service take precedence and supersede these measures. The voluntary slowdown is led by the Quiet Sound program at Maritime Blue, in cooperation with government agencies, tribal governments, industry partners and conservation groups. For more detailed information related to this slowdown and the Quiet Sound program, including a graphic of the voluntary slowdown area, refer to the following web address: https://quietsound.org/admiralty-inlet-slowdown.

w.t:

General / Threatened And Endangered Species Advisory (TESS Advisory) / Marine Wildlife Migration
Effective 15 June until 23:59hrs PST on 30 Nov 2026, the Enhancing Cetacean Habitat and Observation (ECHO) Program voluntary ship slowdown through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass is in effect for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales. If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water: 11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and, 14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels. This voluntary slowdown takes place between 48°24'22.78"N, 123°12'15.26"W, and 48°46'39.28"N 123°1'36.84"W. Speed transition zones are in place within the established traffic system at both approaches to the slowdown area. The north transition zone are those waters between north of Boat Pass, Saturna Island and Rosenfeld Rock and the south transition zone are those waters between buoy VH at the Victoria pilot station, and Sea Bird Point at the southeast corner of Discovery Island. There are also two optional slow down areas, one rounding turn point and the other between Turn point, Saturna Island and Alden Point, Patos Island. This initiative will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 23:59 PDT on 30 Nov 2026, depending on southern resident killer whale presence in the fall. The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups. For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address: ECHO Program’s 2026 voluntary slowdowns and route alteration for commercial ships | Vancouver Fraser Port Authority

Pile driving and setting of precast concrete during new construction phases. - Hazards to Mariners: Turbidity curtain around the work area. Barges positioned at the head of the existing pier and secured to the creek bed with spuds. Trestle extending into the waterway parallel to the existing pier and future new pier. One 25' tug. The Sevenson Environmental Services and PGE will be conducting environmental dredging and installing steel piles from 19 May, 2026 - 30 November, 2026. Operation times will be five to six days per week, with hours of operations 5am to 7pm(local). This operation will include the use the following vessels and equipment: 40x80 PC650-01, 40x80 PC650-02, Crane Barge MICHEAL LIND, Staging barge STELLA LIND, Tug CASSIE LIND, Tug ARCHIE LIND, SEVENSON 01 and 02 work boats. All vessels and equipment on site will monitor VHF-FM Channels 13, 14 and operating on 11. Sevenson will utilize two 40x80 barges with PC650 excavators on them to perform environmental dredging and capping via clam shell bucket and conventional buckets. Sevenson has hired Lind marine to subcontract out work including the transloading operations via E-Crane “Greta Jean Lind”. The Michael Lind (Crane Barge) will be in the area for support, along with another spud barge “Stella Lind” for staging room. Steel pipe pile will be installed roughly up to 400 ft offshore to hold the turbidity curtain. During the project, we will also install 504 wooden piles for slope stability. The PC650 will load into 6x – 100CY (30’ x 40’) scows and pushed to the edge of the curtain. From there the E-Crane will take the material and transload into large Jumbo Hoppers. Lind Marine will use the Cassie Lind (1200 HP tug) to push the scows up to Birds Landing, CA to an offload facility. At the offload facility there will be an E-Crane to offload the material from the scows onto land. Lind Marine will use the Cassie Lind (1200 HP tug) to push the scows up to Birds Landing, CA to an offload facility. At the offload facility there will be an E-Crane to offload the material from the scows onto land. Lind Marine will also use the Cassie Lind to push scows to Redwood City, CA to an offload facility. w.t:
SACRAMENTO RIVER DEEP WATER SHIP CHANNEL - SACRAMENTO RIVER
General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Facilities, Barriers, Manmade Reefs, Riprap, Jetties / Dikes
Contractors for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will conduct marine operations for levee rehabilitation along the Sacramento River between River Miles 47.3 and 53.5 . Waterside work is scheduled to begin July 6, 2026, and will continue through approximately November 30, 2026. Operations will involve up to three crane barges (including Crane Barge #12, measuring approximately 140' x 50'), a tugboat, two workboats, and a rotation of flat deck barges. Work will occur during daylight hours; however, barge maneuvering outside the construction area may occur 24 hours a day. Flat deck barges will transit between the job site and the San Rafael Rock Quarry, utilizing pre-existing moorings along the Sacramento River, including locations at River Miles 26 and 27 near Walnut Grove, CA. At the end of each shift, barges will be spudded in place and marked with steady burning white lights on all corners. Mariners are advised to use extreme caution, transit at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake, and maintain a safe distance. Project vessels will monitor VHF-FM channels 9, 16, and 68A, and can be contacted directly at (707) 333-5029.

When the bascule span of the highway bridge is in the closed-to-navigation position and the lift span of the railroad bridge is in the partially open position, providing 80 feet of vertical clearance at mean high water, the lift span center channel navigation lights will show a red 180-degree center span light on the upstream and downstream lower edge of the span. 2. When the bascule span of the highway bridge is in the fully opened position and the lift span of the railroad bridge is in the fully opened position, providing 135 feet of vertical clearance at mean high water, the lift span center channel navigation lights will show two solid 360-degree green lights on the upstream and downstream lower edge of the span, providing a range for the centerline of the channel between both highway and railroad bridges.
